s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, painless, periocular swelling with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis on histopathology
Soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid on CT scan
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
Several-month history of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema
History of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
Left levator resection for ptosis
Dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
Mass persisted despite two courses of antibiotics
Nodule remained stable in size three months after surgery
Focal, non-tender, indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim on examination
CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening without extension into surrounding structures or bony invasion
Excisional biopsy performed
Intraoperative frozen sections revealed granulomatous inflammation
Final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin
No evidence of malignancy on histopathology
Bacterial and fungal stains (Ziehl–Neelsen and Grocott) were negative

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, painless, periocular swelling with granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation with extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and history of chronic scleritis

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema on the face

raw.rationale: The presence of granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis, extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin, and scattered multinucleated giant cells, along with a history of chronic scleritis and the absence of malignancy or infection, is most consistent with IgG4-related disease, which is known for its involvement of various organs including the orbit and its characteristic histopathological features.

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: Lack of specific histopathological features and a broader differential diagnosis

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and non-caseating granulomas without necrobiosis

rejected.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: Characterized by the presence of xanthoma cells and typically associated with paraproteinemia, not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Typically presents as a brownish plaque on the face, especially the forehead, nose, or cheeks, and lacks the specific histopathological features seen in this case
